model¶

Public API for conditional transformation models.

Users import exclusively from this module:

import pymlt
model = pymlt.MLT(order=6, support=(0, 100))
model.fit(y)
cdf = model.predict(y_new, what="distribution")

Classes¶

ConditionalTransformationModel

Base class for all transformation models.

MLT

Most Likely Transformation — convenience subclass with sensible defaults.

class pymlt.model.ConditionalTransformationModel(basis, censoring=CensoringType.NONE, optimizer_config=None, base_distribution='normal')[source]¶

Bases: object

Base class for conditional transformation models.

Fits a monotone transformation h(y|x) parametrised as a Bernstein polynomial such that h(y|x) follows a standard distribution.

Parameters:

  • basis (BernsteinBasis) – BernsteinBasis defining the response transformation.

  • censoring (CensoringType) – Censoring type of the response data. Defaults to NONE.

  • optimizer_config (OptimizerConfig | None) – Optimisation settings. If None, defaults from OptimizerConfig are used.

theta_¶

Fitted parameter vector [theta_basis | beta]. None before fit().

Type:

NDArray or None

result_¶

Full result object from the last fit() call. None before fit().

Type:

OptimizationResult or None

is_fitted_¶

Whether fit() has been called successfully.

Type:

bool

Parameters:

base_distribution (Literal['normal', 'logistic', 'min_extreme_value'])

fit(y, X=None)[source]¶

Fit the transformation model by maximum likelihood.

Parameters:

  • y (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | CensoredData) – Response observations. Must lie within basis.support. Accepts np.ndarray, pd.Series, or CensoredData.

  • X (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional covariate matrix of shape (n, q). If given, the last q entries of theta_ are regression coefficients.

Returns:

Returns itself for method chaining:

cdf = model.fit(y).predict(y, what="distribution")

Return type:

ConditionalTransformationModel

Raises:

ValueError – If y contains values outside basis.support.

predict(y_new, X_new=None, what='distribution')[source]¶

Compute model predictions at new observations.

Parameters:

  • y_new (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]) – For what ∈ {"distribution", "density", "hazard"}: response values in basis.support. For what="quantile": probabilities in (0, 1).

  • X_new (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional covariate matrix of shape (m, q).

  • what (Literal['distribution', 'density', 'quantile', 'hazard']) –

    Type of prediction:

    • "distribution" — CDF: F(h(y|x))

    • "density" — PDF: f(h(y|x)) · h’(y|x)

    • "quantile" — Quantile via numerical inversion (brentq)

    • "hazard" — Hazard: f(h)/F̄(h); only for censoring=RIGHT

Return type:

ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]

Raises:

  • NotFittedError – If called before fit().

  • ValueError – If what is not one of the valid options.

  • NotImplementedError – If what="hazard" and censoring is not RIGHT.

Examples

>>> model = MLT(order=4, support=(0, 1)).fit(y)
>>> cdf = model.predict(y_new, what="distribution")
>>> q50 = model.predict(np.array([0.5]), what="quantile")
score(y, X=None)[source]¶

Log-likelihood at the fitted parameters (sklearn-compatible).

Higher is better; this is NOT the negative log-likelihood.

Parameters:

  • y (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | CensoredData) – Response observations.

  • X (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional covariate matrix.

Return type:

float

Raises:

NotFittedError – If called before fit().

simulate(n, X=None, random_state=None)[source]¶

Draw samples from the fitted model via the quantile transformation.

Samples u ~ Uniform(0, 1) and returns predict(u, X, what="quantile").

Parameters:

  • n (int) – Number of samples to draw.

  • X (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional covariate matrix of shape (n, q).

  • random_state (int | Generator | None) – Seed or numpy.random.Generator for reproducibility.

Return type:

ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]

Raises:

NotFittedError – If called before fit().

exception pymlt.model.ConvergenceWarning[source]¶

Bases: UserWarning

Raised when the optimiser fails to converge within the allowed restarts.

class pymlt.model.MLT(order=6, support=(0.0, 1.0), censoring=CensoringType.NONE, optimizer_config=None, base_distribution='normal')[source]¶

Bases: ConditionalTransformationModel

Most Likely Transformation — convenience interface.

A ConditionalTransformationModel with an explicit order and support parameter instead of a pre-built BernsteinBasis.

Parameters:

  • order (int) – Polynomial degree of the Bernstein basis. Defaults to 6.

  • support (tuple[float, float]) – Closed interval (a, b) with a < b. Defaults to (0, 1).

  • censoring (CensoringType) – Censoring type of the response data.

  • optimizer_config (OptimizerConfig | None) – Optimisation settings.

Examples

>>> model = MLT(order=6, support=(0, 100))
>>> model.fit(y)
>>> cdf = model.predict(y_new, what="distribution")
Parameters:

base_distribution (Literal['normal', 'logistic', 'min_extreme_value'])

exception pymlt.model.NotFittedError[source]¶

Bases: ValueError

Raised when a method that requires a fitted model is called before fit().
